items.title: Building a language tutor with Codex (and zero mobile experience)
items.guest_line: William Imoh · Founder @ Hackmamba (developer marketing company); captions say "William Emo", spelling taken from the episode notes. Host: Claire Vo
items.vendor_flag: Guest is not selling the tools praised (Codex, GPT-Live, ChatGPT). His own app Mural is free and open source by his account; he mentions Hackmamba's growth services at the end. Sponsor reads for WorkOS (1:42) and Vanta (20:02) sit outside the discussion.
items.reader_fit: Low to moderate: mostly a builder story, but the candidate logging and ranking workflow after each call and the weekly start, stop, keep brief translate to an off-the-shelf assistant with email and calendar access.

points.claim: After a candidate call, one instruction gets the assistant to pull email, calendar and meeting notes into his people system, summarise, score and rank the candidate
points.evidence: Internal tool the captions call "three pipes"; example rank seven of 15 candidates spoken to
points.quote: It goes sc my email, my calendar, looks at meeting notes, collects all that information, puts it in three pipes, gives me a summary, it's all done, and then scores the candidate as well

points.claim: A real-time voice tutor session costs a few dollars per half hour to run
points.evidence: $3 to $5 per 30 minutes on OpenAI GPT-Live; $1,000 budget with about $100 left
points.quote: It's going to cost between three and $5 for 30 minutes.

points.claim: He briefs the coding agent with design references and a strict minimalism rule rather than technical specs
points.evidence: Codex building Swift for iOS and Kotlin for Android; never written Swift
points.quote: No element on the screen should exist unless it absolutely has to.

points.claim: A weekly routine produces an operator brief with start, stop, keep and the three highest impact activities
points.evidence: Every Sunday night, run as a routine in ChatGPT projects
points.quote: I also ask you for like the three highest impact activities I would conduct this week.

points.claim: Agents get access to everything except write access to the bank, plus no customer data
points.evidence: 15 to 16 browser tabs connected, including Linear, Notion, calendar, Pipedrive and QuickBooks (caption spelling garbled)
points.quote: The only thing it doesn't have right access to is the bank.

points.claim: Long gamified app streaks did not produce conversational ability
points.evidence: 1,000 day Duolingo streak
points.quote: I had a thousand day streak on Dualingo.

items.title: I was a Claude hater. Fable 5.2 changed my mind.
items.guest_line: No guest: host-only episode. Claire Vo · Host @ How I AI, founder @ ChatPRD
items.vendor_flag: No guest. Host praises Anthropic's Fable 5.2 after early access (she thanks the Anthropic team); no sponsor read in the transcript. Demos feature her own products (ChatPRD, CXO.dev).
items.reader_fit: Low: model launch impressions aimed at builders. The one recruiter takeaway is turning a post plus brand guidelines into an animated video, and the routing advice (Opus 5.5 for daily work) is useful context only.

points.claim: Anthropic positions Opus 5.5 for everyday work and Fable 5.2 for scope, complexity and creativity
points.evidence: Fable 5.2 vs Opus 5.5, Anthropic guidance relayed by host
points.quote: they say most daily coding and knowledge tasks are Opus 55 tasks
points.attributed_to: Anthropic, as relayed by Claire Vo

points.claim: A single tweet plus brand guidelines became a fully animated video without storyboarding
points.evidence: CXO.dev brand guidelines; prompt "Make this tweet a video"
points.quote: I gave Fable that tweet plus our CXO.dev brand guidelines and said, "Make this tweet a video."

points.claim: Unguided, the model's web design is poor; it needs a brand or style guide
points.evidence: Weak at front end and web design
points.quote: left to its own devices, it has incredibly concerning taste

points.claim: It produced correct flat-pack assembly order from low resolution photos where every other model failed
points.evidence: 25 pieces of wood, no instructions
points.quote: it showed up with an open bag of screws, 25 pieces of wood and no instructions

points.claim: Speed on her own benchmark: complex animation in 16 minutes, many tasks under a minute
points.evidence: 16 minutes; sub 1 minute; host's own How I AI bench, not independent
points.quote: even something as complex as animating the invader bots only took 16 minutes

points.claim: Anthropic says Fable 5.2 solved two open problems in black hole physics
points.evidence: Two open problems; Anthropic launch claim, not tested by host
points.quote: it solved two open problems in the physics of black holes
points.attributed_to: Anthropic, as relayed by Claire Vo

items.title: Claude Code + Obsidian: My family's AI brain
items.guest_line: Scott Farrar · maths teacher and parent (site sfxmath.com); employer not stated. Host: Claire Vo
items.vendor_flag: Guest is not behind any product praised (Claude Code, Obsidian, Dropbox, Dakboard). Sponsor reads for WorkOS (0:52) and Jira Product Discovery (18:04) sit outside the discussion.
items.reader_fit: Low to moderate: the content is household admin, but the method (a folder of plain notes an AI agent keeps up to date, with project checklists and a prioritised to-do file) transfers to a recruiter's own roles and clients. It assumes comfort with a desktop agent like Claude Code.

points.claim: Moving from web chat to a coding agent that reads and writes markdown files keeps the AI grounded in the same context across sessions
points.evidence: Claude Code, markdown files viewed in Obsidian
points.quote: I built this system that would read and write files, read and write markdown files, so they would have the memory of what we were talking about

points.claim: Asking the AI what to gather first produced a concrete collection task
points.evidence: Photograph every appliance; summarised into an appliances list
points.quote: go around and take pictures of of every appliance in your house

points.claim: A shared brain dump of tasks is turned into a prioritised, costed to-do file
points.evidence: Priority level, cost estimate and reference per item
points.quote: give me a priority level, give me a a a cost estimate

points.claim: Project checklists and overdue reminders cleared his backlog
points.evidence: Example reminder: waiting since 24 September
points.quote: it's going to remind me that you've been waiting since September 24th on this

points.claim: He set hard scope limits on what goes into the system
points.evidence: No finances, no medical information
points.quote: I'm not going to do finances with this. I'm not doing medical information.

points.claim: A script pushes priorities and a recent wins section to a wall display
points.evidence: Dakboard custom web page
points.quote: I also put made a section of recent wins just to say like good job.

items.title: How I fight token fraud as an AI founder
items.guest_line: No guest: host-only episode. Claire Vo · Host @ How I AI, solo founder @ ChatPRD (captions garble the product name as "Chat Purity", "Chaparral", "Chat Proxy")
items.vendor_flag: Host is the founder of the product under attack. She praises Stripe Radar, Vercel AI Gateway, BotID and firewall, and Clerk; WorkOS is this episode's sponsor and she thanks Michael at WorkOS in the main content (20:45 and 28:44), and Persona is named as a past sponsor. Sponsor read for Auros (captions "Oros", 19:50) sits outside the discussion.
items.reader_fit: Low: written for founders selling AI software. The transferable point for a recruiter is that a candidate-facing chatbot or AI agent should never be given the power to grant access or exceptions, and that free tiers of AI tools are tightening.

points.claim: Token fraud has cost the business tens of thousands of dollars in roughly a year
points.evidence: Tens of thousands of dollars; ChatPRD, bootstrapped
points.quote: This has cost me tens of thousands of dollars over I would say the past year.

points.claim: She ended free trials because no cost-effective free tier survived abuse, at the price of losing a lead source
points.evidence: Free trials were a source of PLG and enterprise leads
points.quote: the biggest lever we could pull is we just turned off free trials

points.claim: An AI support desk needs fraud tools but must not be allowed to unban, ban or hand out promo codes
points.evidence: Fraud lists, allow lists, playbooks
points.quote: people will try to use your AI support desk as a vector of attack

points.claim: Flagged chats are classified by a cheap decision model, then banned or silently downgraded to a cheaper model
points.evidence: OpenAI decision model the captions call "Jev" (exact name unclear); categories include trial abuse, promo abuse, card fraud, resale, agent farming
points.quote: we ban them or we silent downgrade them to like a GLM

points.claim: A card testing attack showed about $200,000 of attempted purchases, all failed
points.evidence: $200,000 attempted; caught with Stripe Radar
points.quote: I woke up one day and saw that like $200,000 had been um attempted purchases

points.claim: Billing and payment controls: charge up front with no grace period
points.evidence: Advice credited to Gareth at Atlassian
points.quote: So you have to charge up front, no grace period on failed payments, nothing.
points.attributed_to: Gareth at Atlassian, relayed by Claire Vo
